ceilingNote: Derived from the ABS v4 capture (max measured run + largest single request). That run is 49 turns of DeepSWE, whereas LHTB averages ~9.9M tokens/task, so this ceiling is roughly one sixth of a full-length LHTB run. It is deliberately short: loop 3 is looking for winning patterns cheaply. No published claim may rest on it, and the real batch must derive its ceiling from a completed LHTB pilot.
transportNote: Reply cap and request timeout are one decision, derived not guessed. Measured: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash generates at 52.7 tok/s (4,096 completion tokens in 77.7s, isolated probe). The harness leaves AGENT_MAX_TOKENS unset by design -- "a host that genuinely needs a bound passes one" -- and this is such a host: an uncapped reply on a task that asks the agent to write a whole pipeline runs for minutes and exceeds any timeout, which voided three loop3 arms. 8,192 tokens is ~600 lines per turn, generous for one reply, and bounds generation at ~155s; the 300s timeout gives 1.9x headroom, so a call exceeding it is genuinely hung rather than merely slow. The runner refuses a timeout without a cap, and refuses a timeout below what a full reply needs at this rate. The cap applies to EVERY arm -- the attention arm previously set none at all, so the comparison was not at parity.
substrateNote: Substrate switched from z-ai/glm-5.3-flash to qwen/qwen3.7-flash for two independent reasons, both measured. (1) SPEED AND SAFETY: measured generation rates over two 4,096-token trials each -- qwen 75.7/84.2 tok/s, deepseek 66.3/98.3, glm 26.4/24.5. GLM is ~3x slower and its rate is unstable; at its slowest observed 24.5 tok/s a full 8,192-token reply needs 335s, which EXCEEDS the 300s timeout, so legitimate full-length replies were still being killed. An earlier single GLM probe read 52.7 tok/s, which is why the 300s timeout looked sufficient -- one sample of a variable rate. Qwen needs 108s for the same reply, giving 2.8x headroom. (2) ECONOMICS, which matters more: qwen3.7-flash is the ONLY cheap OpenRouter model in the price table with a nonzero cacheWrite (0.038 against input 0.03, i.e. 1.27x). GLM and deepseek publish cacheWrite 0, a free-prefix-rewrite edge case that flatters ejection. Qwen therefore has real eviction economics: its break-even is 6.3 turns against GLM 5.0 and Anthropic 12.5, so results transfer far better. The ejection cadence moves from 5 to 6 accordingly. CAVEAT: the price table holds qwen3.7-flash base tier and notes tiered overrides above 32k prompt tokens, so dollar figures on runs exceeding 32k prompt are underestimates; tokens remain the primary effort endpoint and are unaffected.
